title: How to Dance Afro Fusion | Beginner's Dance Workshop in Gweta

observation_window.sampling: provider default; not continuous motion capture

extraction.teacher_style: Patience J is energetic, encouraging, and breaks down movements step-by-step from upper body to footwork. She emphasizes personal style and expression while practicing with two assistants in the studio.

lesson_structure.note: Patience J introduces herself and the two participants, Bella and Ranjini.
Explains the groove Gweta from Togo and its meaning.
Teaches the upper body arm movement.
Teaches the lower body footwork side to side.
Combines upper and lower body with a wiggle-wiggle effect.
Practices the dance routine with music at a slow and then faster tempo.

cues: Pick up a key and place it down
metaphors: Imagining you're picking up a key and you're just placing it down
Imagine a wave and something smooth

steps_taught.name: Gweta Upper Body
steps_taught.description: Picking up and placing a key side to side with a ripple effect.

steps_taught.name: Gweta Footwork
steps_taught.description: Stepping side to side and dropping into the rhythm.

what_works: Breaking down the upper body and feet separately before combining
Demonstrating with two assistants so viewers see group context

quotes.text: Don't forget you can adapt anything you learn today.
The essence of this dance is equivalent to dodging jealous people.
Don't be afraid to go that further with the body.
Give it your own flavor, add your personality into it.

evidence_segments.observation: Teacher stands centrally facing camera with two participants flanking her in a dance studio.
Teacher demonstrates arm movements while explaining key-placement metaphor, followed by assistants copying.
Teacher demonstrates footwork stepping side to side with subtle knee bobs.
evidence_segments.cannot_infer: exact foot placement details due to trousers

evidence_segments.observation: Group dances together to music while teacher counts and verbally encourages.

extraction.distinctive_method: Associating cultural context and storytelling ('dodging jealous people') directly with the movement meaning ('Gweta').
